summary: Editor and shader tooling done and verified. Builder.cs (contract 17 + 23.3): SetupAndCompile, BuildWindows, BuildAndroid, BuildAll, -buildOut <dir> override (defaults Build/Windows, Build/Android; BuildAll uses <dir>/Windows and <dir>/Android), -development flag, layer 31 LiquidField, Scenes/Main.unity with one GameObject Game + GameDirector (B0a type, referenced directly), PlayerSettings (Painter IO / PainterIO, portrait, windowed 540x960 resizable, no splash, Windows Mono, Android com.painterio.game IL2CPP ARM64 minSdk 25 Vulkan then GLES3, Input System only), quality levels PC->PC_RPAsset (Standalone) and Mobile->Mobile_RPAsset (Android), PC_RPAsset requireDepthTexture/requireOpaqueTexture false, Mobile_RPAsset supportsHDR false, URP shadows and additional lights off, build target restore, VIBRATE Gradle callback under #if UNITY_ANDROID plus an APK manifest check, explicit exit codes, artifact existence checks. ShaderCheck.cs: contract 12.1 checks for .shader and .shadergraph (forced sync import, every pass compiled, ShaderHasError, Error messages, errors logged during import, InternalErrorShader, _PIO_ShaderId marker, no other _PIO_* property, graph shader name, duplicate names, .hlsl without .meta, Custom Function GUID resolution and function presence) and a fix for a batch-mode false green found here: before any camera renders, URP subshaders are unsupported and Shader Graph's FallbackError (1 pass, queue 2000) was what got compiled. ShaderCheck now renders one warm-up frame and asserts the active subshader is the URP one (graphs now compile their real 6 passes). Initial LiquidCommon.hlsl (guard, all _PIO_* globals, PIO_Height exactly as 12.2, first PIO_ShadeLiquid), FieldBlob.shader and FieldStroke.shader (exact blend state, tags, mesh conventions, _PIO_ActorScale, marker). Thin Shader Graph templates ThinUnlitOpaque and ThinUnlitTransparent (URP Unlit, ZTest Always, ZWrite ForceDisabled, one File-mode Custom Function reading vertex color, uv1 and the _PIO_PlayerFade global) proven to import (ShaderCheck.RunTemplates) AND render: ShaderCheck.RenderTemplatesBatch renders each template into a RenderTexture in batch mode and checks exact pixel values (ZTest Always, ZWrite off, alpha blend, global and vertex data paths), and also proves FieldBlob/FieldStroke against the 12.2 formulas in a half-float RT (additive alpha as data, _PIO_ActorScale). docs/SHADERGRAPH_TEMPLATE.md tells B1/B2 exactly how to clone a template. Verified: SetupAndCompile PASS (exit 0), RenderTemplatesBatch PASS (exit 0), BuildWindows -buildOut Build/B0b produced PainterIO.exe which ran B0a's DevShot to the end (scenario PASS, 7 PNGs, quit 0, no exception in player.log; frames are uniform navy because the render views are still stubs), BuildAndroid produced Build/B0b/PainterIO.apk (31.7 MB, VIBRATE inserted by the callback and found in the APK manifest) and restored the Windows target (next editor run compiled with the Windows editor DAG).

contract_issues: Section 19 says all RTs have 'no depth'. URP 17 Render Graph refuses a camera output RenderTexture without a depth buffer: the camera draws nothing and only logs 'In the render graph API, the output Render Texture must have a depth buffer' and 'Fake or uninitialized surface is not supported for attachment 0'. The ActorFieldCamera target _PIO_ActorField therefore needs a depth buffer (16 bit is enough, e.g. new RenderTextureDescriptor(w, h, GraphicsFormat.R16G16B16A16_SFloat, 16)). Reproduced in ShaderCheck.RenderFieldContributors: all zeros without depth, exact values with it. CommandBuffer passes (TerritoryBlur) are not concerned.

Section 12.1's ShaderCheck procedure (new Material(s), CompilePass for each pass) gives a false green in batch mode: until a camera renders, the URP pipeline instance does not exist, Shader.globalRenderPipeline is empty, every RenderPipeline=UniversalPipeline subshader is unsupported and a Shader Graph runs its FallBack 'Hidden/Shader Graph/FallbackError' (1 pass, queue 2000) while still exposing _PIO_ShaderId, so the marker check passes and only the fallback gets compiled (a Transparent graph even reports queue 2000). ShaderCheck now warms URP up with one camera render and fails when the active subshader is not tagged UniversalPipeline or its pass count differs from the material's. Any other editor-side shader check must do the same.

Section 17 puts the IPostGenerateGradleAndroidProject under #if UNITY_ANDROID: it only exists when the editor's active target is Android at compile time, so BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer(Android) from an editor opened on Windows never runs it. BuildAndroid must be started with -buildTarget Android (done here: the callback ran and inserted VIBRATE). Builder also checks the final APK's binary manifest for android.permission.VIBRATE in every case, and BuildAndroid switches back to StandaloneWindows64 afterwards, even when it was started on Android, so the next editor run of any agent opens on Windows.
open_issues: The tests counted above are editor batch checks, not NUnit tests (the test asmdefs belong to other packages): ShaderCheck.RenderTemplates (2 templates x 3 regions, exact colors) and ShaderCheck.RenderFieldContributors (11 pixel samples against the 12.2 formulas). Both PASS. Re-run: tools/unity.ps1 -UnityArgs "run . --timeout 1800 -- -executeMethod PainterIO.Editor.ShaderCheck.RenderTemplatesBatch -shotDir TestResults -logFile Logs/<you>_render.log".

The templates are proven in the editor only (batch render on the editor D3D12 device). They live outside Resources and never ship, by design. FieldBlob and FieldStroke are compiled into the Windows and Android players (build log), but no player draws them yet: LiquidRenderer and the actor views are still stubs, so the DevShot PNGs from Build/B0b are uniform navy (#151D38 clear). The liquid look against docs/reference_gouttes.png is for B1/B2 to judge.

PIO_ShadeLiquid is a reasonable first version (wrapped Lambert, Blinn-Phong gloss 100, optional broad lobe, Fresnel rim, meniscus foot darkening, thin-liquid brightening). B1 owns its tuning from now on.
The APK was built but not installed on a device (no device attached).

On this Intel iGPU the Windows player picks D3D11 ('D3D12 API denied by user filter'), while the editor uses D3D12. The render checks therefore ran on D3D12 and the player on D3D11. FYI only, no problem seen.
